newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian Malev expands cargo facilities.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian Malev expands cargo facilities.

text.p: Hungarian national airline Malev Rt said on Thursday it will build cargo facilities near the planned expansion of the second terminal at Ferihegy Airport in Budapest.
"We will have brand new cargo facilities," Ferenc Kovacs, Malev's cargo manager, told Reuters. "We have to do this to grow -- we'll start losing business if we don't."
Malev has not decided on the building's cost and size, but facilities will include cargo warehouses as well as office space for airlines, customs officials and freight forwarders, Kovacs said.
No opening date for the new building has been determined, but Hungary's airport and air traffic administration LRI said it expects the expanded terminal to be completed in 1998.
Ferihegy's second terminal opened in 1985, but Malev's cargo operations currently are at the airport's first terminal, which opened in 1950.

Malev is owned 63.9 percent by the Hungarian State Privatisation and Asset Holding Co (APV Rt), 30.0 percent by Italian airline Alitalia, 5.0 percent by the Italian ministry of foreign trade's investment agency SIMEST, and 1.1 percent by other interests, including Hungarian municipalities.
